forum.title: 9 axis only gyroscope mems sensor available?
forum.best_answer_content:
Well, that’s the range of sensors which ST has.

If you don’t see anything there suitable for your (unstated) application requirements, then you’ll obviously have to look elsewhere.

But, as ​@TDK said, we live in a 3D world - so any real gyro can only have 3 axes

**PS:**

You can combine an LSM6DSOX + LIS3MDL to give you 9 DOF; eg,

<https://www.adafruit.com/product/4517>

Other sensors, of course, can be used: [Basics of 6DOF and 9DOF sensor fusion](https://embeddedcomputing.com/technology/analog-and-power/basics-of-6dof-and-9dof-sensor-fusion)

PPS:

See also:

<https://community.st.com/mems-sensors-48/9-axis-sensor-fusion-implementation-dt0058-dt0060-161638>

which refers to:

Design tip [**DT0058**](https://www.st.com/resource/en/design_tip/dt0058-computing-tilt-measurement-and-tiltcompensated-ecompass-stmicroelectronics.pdf), *Computing tilt measurement and tilt-compensated eCompass*

Design tip [**DT0060**](https://www.st.com/resource/en/design_tip/dt0060-exploiting-the-gyroscope-to-update-tilt-measurement-and-ecompass-stmicroelectronics.pdf), *Exploiting the gyroscope to update tilt measurement and eCompass*
forum.author: Kalpesh salunke

scraped_replies.html: It's 3 axis gyroscope u have send , i wanna know if 6 or 9 axis gyroscope mems exit for phones
scraped_replies.author: Kalpesh salunke

scraped_replies.html: As the space we mortals inhabit is three dimensional, you will only see up to 3-axis gyroscopes here on Earth. Perhaps you are confusing this with a 9-DOF sensor.
